option_relations.rationale: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with cervical osteophyte-induced dysphagia is a specific presentation of Cervical osteophyte syndrome, where the osteophytes cause dysphagia.

Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with hypoglossal nerve palsy is a specific manifestation of Cervical osteophyte syndrome, where the osteophytes cause hypoglossal nerve palsy. This is a subtype of the broader syndrome.

Cervical osteophyte-induced dysphagia (Forestier’s disease) is another name for Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) causing dysphagia, which is a specific presentation of Cervical osteophyte syndrome.
Degenerative cervical spine disease is a broader category that can encompass Cervical osteophyte syndrome, but the latter is more specific to the osteophyte-related symptoms.
